recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the FHIR-33309 clarification in the current search page without reopening or broadening later search-parameter changes.
issue_request: FHIR-33309 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core-search and requested that wildcard _include/_revinclude wording not imply every ordinary reference search parameter is included, but only those supported for _include/_revinclude.
initial_application: Commit 01625dddcaabfbbe98974ea9eb5563a2e6b2979f applied FHIR-33309 to the syntax bullets in source/search.html by referring to supported references and adding a note that include/revinclude support can differ from ordinary search-parameter support. That commit did not update the later paragraph that directly repeated the issue's quoted ambiguous wording.
additional_context: The originating Zulip thread #implementers > _include=* records the same ambiguity and the filing of J#33309, and FHIR-I minutes from 2021-11-29 record approval to add the proposed clarification. Later Applied issue FHIR-50714 updated the same search page to include resource-type search parameters and rewrote the later wildcard paragraph, so this reconciliation preserves that later resource-type scope while adding the missing support qualification.
reconciliation: Updated source/search.html, the active FHIR-core search page source, so the later wildcard paragraph says the wildcard includes search parameters of type reference or resource only when they are supported for _include or _revinclude. No other source changes were needed because the nearby syntax bullet already carries the support-scope note.
source_changes: source/search.html: clarified the later _include/_revinclude wildcard paragraph to require that type=reference or type=resource search parameters be supported for _include or _revinclude before they are included by wildcard.

related_jiras.note: This later Applied issue updated the same search-page area to include resource-type search parameters; the FHIR-33309 fix preserves that later addition.
